acceptance_criteria: cargo test -p stoa-mail passes; dev-mode + non-loopback in mail is fatal; verify_http_signatures=false + non-loopback is fatal; clippy clean
description:
## What
In crates/mail/src/main.rs, upgrade two existing warn! guards to fatal eprintln! + process::exit(1):
1. auth dev-mode (is_dev_mode()) on non-loopback → fatal (currently only warns for operator_usernames case)
2. activitypub.enabled && !verify_http_signatures on non-loopback → fatal (currently just warn)

## Algorithm
1. Read crates/mail/src/main.rs fully.
2. Add is_loopback_addr helper to crates/mail/src/config.rs — use stoa_core::util::is_loopback_addr if W0A landed, otherwise add a local copy with the same body.
3. At startup (after tracing init, before credential_store build), add:
   if config.auth.is_dev_mode() && !is_loopback_addr(&config.listen.jmap_addr) {
       eprintln!('error: stoa-mail is configured in dev mode (auth.required = false, no users configured) but is listening on a non-loopback address ({addr}). ...');
       process::exit(1);
   }
   Note: mail config may have jmap_addr or http_addr — check the exact field name in config.rs.
4. For verify_http_signatures:
   Change lines ~249-255 from:
     warn!('...')
   to:
     if config.activitypub.enabled && !config.activitypub.verify_http_signatures
         && !is_loopback_addr(&config.listen.jmap_addr)
     {
         eprintln!('error: stoa-mail: activitypub.verify_http_signatures = false disables HTTP signature verification, allowing any actor to forge inbound ActivityPub activities. Set verify_http_signatures = true or bind to 127.0.0.1.');
         process::exit(1);
     }
5. cargo fmt; cargo clippy clean; cargo test --workspace clean.

## Defensive programming rules
- Read the exact listen.addr field name from crates/mail/src/config.rs before writing — do not guess.
- No unwrap().
- Error messages must be actionable and must NOT contain any auth credentials or tokens.

## Tests
Add to crates/mail/src/config.rs tests:
- test_mail_dev_mode_nonloopback: is_dev_mode()=true + non-loopback → condition = true. Oracle: guard condition logic.
- test_mail_dev_mode_loopback: is_dev_mode()=true + loopback → condition = false. Oracle: loopback is safe.
- test_activitypub_noverify_nonloopback: enabled=true, verify_http_signatures=false, non-loopback → condition = true. Oracle: guard condition logic.
- test_activitypub_noverify_loopback: same but loopback → condition = false.
title: mail: fatal guards for dev-mode and verify_http_signatures=false
